title: 👑 Elite Challenge: Mastering Word Building & Linking Words

questions.prompt: Someone made this jacket well. Which phrase describes it?
questions.explanation: The pattern is adverb + hyphen + past participle: well + made gives "a well-made jacket". The adverb comes first, so "made-well" is in the wrong order; "good" is an adjective, not an adverb; and "making" is not a past participle.

questions.prompt: Answer: "Ali went home early because he felt sick." Ask about the reason.

options.text: Why did Ali go home early?
How did Ali go home early?
Why did Ali went home early?

questions.explanation: A reason is asked with "why". The verb "went" is in the past, so the helper is "did" and the verb returns to its base form "go": Why did Ali go home early? "How" would ask about the manner, and "did… went" marks the past twice.

questions.prompt: Complete: "While ___ fruit is healthy, ___ too many sweets can harm your teeth."
questions.explanation: Each part of the contrast has a verb as its subject, and a verb used as a subject takes the gerund: While eating fruit is healthy, eating too many sweets can harm your teeth. The bare verb "eat" cannot be a subject, and mixing forms breaks the parallel between the two opposite ideas.

questions.prompt: Find the sentence with a linking mistake.

options.text: The air is polluted because factories release fumes.
The water is dirty. Therefore, it is not safe to drink.
Because the road was icy, so the bus stopped.
It was very hot, so we stayed inside.

questions.explanation: The mistake is "Because…, so…": English uses ONE linker for one link. Correct it with "The road was icy, so the bus stopped" or "The bus stopped because the road was icy." The other sentences each use one linker, in front of the right part.

questions.prompt: Which compound noun follows the pattern noun + gerund?
questions.explanation: In "wind surfing", "wind" is a noun and "surfing" is a gerund (surf + ing): noun + gerund. "Frying pan" and "driving licence" are the reverse pattern, gerund + noun, and "taxi driver" is noun + -er noun.

questions.prompt: Complete: "Sara and Rim built ___ robot ___, with no help."
questions.explanation: Before the noun "robot" we need the possessive adjective "their" (theirs stands alone, without a noun). "With no help" calls for the reflexive pronoun, and for two people it is "themselves"; "theirselves" does not exist.
